name: Baseline
narrative: The Coastal Bend runs normally, with about 310 911 calls and 520 ER visits a day in Nueces County. Pump P-2 at O.N. Stevens creeps up in vibration and its work order is deferred. MV Halcyon Drift loiters offshore among the crude-export tankers under its true identity, two new vendors register at the same Corpus Christi address, and KESTREL scans the aid portal and NAS Corpus Christi's logistics system. KESTREL also steals remote-access credentials from Brightwake Marine Systems, a vendor that maintains tanker cargo systems, and STATE-X announces naval exercises abroad.

name: Signals
narrative: The seasonal outlook calls for an active season. Rafael forms in the northwestern Caribbean at D-10, crosses the Yucatan into the Gulf, and the forecast cone covers the Coastal Bend by D-5. The Nueces River rises at Calallen and 40 relief containers are booked. NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville fly their aircraft to NAS JRB Fort Worth, and the Army depot secures helicopters in hangars. The Coast Guard sets Port Condition X-Ray at D-3, postponing a Fort Hood aviation brigade outload; the port closes to inbound ships at D-2 (Yankee) with 14 vessels queued offshore, and to all traffic at D-1 (Zulu). KESTREL quietly uses the vendor's access to reach two laden tankers, MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay, which stay moored at an Inner Harbor terminal through the storm.

name: Landfall
narrative: Two hours before landfall, commands sent through the vendor's access open the two tankers' cargo valves and silence their alarms; about 9,000 barrels of crude spill before crews close the valves. Rafael makes landfall on Mustang Island at 06:00Z on D0 as a Category 3 storm, pushing a 3.4 m surge into Corpus Christi and Nueces bays that carries the oil across 85 km² of bay and shoreline. Both power feeds to O.N. Stevens fail three hours later, taking down pumps P-2 and P-3; a citywide boil-water notice follows at D+4. 911 calls peak at 2,900 a day, 61% from low-income surge-zone tracts; the Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway close, and depot hangars take roof damage and water intrusion. KESTREL phishes city and NAS staff, a disinformation network spreads rumors, and both shell vendors win sole-source contracts. Unidentified drones fly over NAS Corpus Christi and the depot on six nights while storm-damaged perimeter sensors are down.

name: Response
narrative: The ship channel partly reopens at D+30, but the anchorage backlog delays MV Gulf Provider and spill cleanup restricts the inner channel until D+44. Halcyon Drift goes dark for 14 hours at D+31, drops two seabed explosive devices off the entrance channel, and transfers fuel to Barge 44, and that fuel reaches NAS Corpus Christi through SUP-0390. Forty relief flights land, pump parts finally arrive at D+36, and the station's backup generator fails on contaminated fuel at D+40. GPS interference from the Inner Harbor disrupts the last relief flights. At D+44, as the outload is about to resume, one device detonates beside a harbor tug at the Port Aransas jetties; the channel closes for mine clearance until D+58, STATE-X moves militarily abroad at D+46, and the Fort Hood outload finally sails from D+59.

name: Recovery
narrative: FEMA approves Individual Assistance on D+57 after delayed damage assessments; registration opens D+60 and takes 48,000 claims in 30 days. KESTREL credential stuffing takes over 410 portal accounts; with six synthetic identities, the ring diverts $3.9M into three bank accounts, two shared with the shell vendors. SUP-0388 bills 2.3× the debris tonnage that imagery supports, and a second disinformation wave claims contractors are stealing aid. Oil spill damage claims from fishers and shoreline owners reach 4,200.

name: Review
narrative: The civilian review finds low-income surge-zone tracts received aid dollars at half their share of residents. The DoD after-action review traces NAS Corpus Christi readiness falling from 92% to 61% and recovering to 85% by D+110. The IC assessment ties KESTREL, the disinformation network and the shell vendors' bank accounts to Halcyon Drift's operator, Brannoch Maritime Holdings, acting for STATE-X. It also attributes the tanker attack and the channel mining to STATE-X, both timed to the storm to spread damage and delay the US deployment. The DoD review adds force-protection gaps: six nights of undetected drone overflights and a channel mined without detection.
